A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
GaN NWs can be grown on Si by molecular beam epitaxy in a self-induced and a collector-induced way.

GaN NWs can grow self-induced on Si(1 11) and Si(00 1) without any external catalyst and that the material quality of these NWs is superior to that of NWs grown on the same substrate by the collector-induced method.

the growth of GaN NWs on Si substrates is a very promising approach for the realization of III-Nitride-based nanoscale devices, in particular if the collector is avoided and the growth temperature is kept high enough to suppress the formation of A-plane facets.

self-induced GaN NWs grown by molecular beam epitaxy on Si(111) are a promising material platform for nanophotonics and optoelectronics.
